stories.title: Former Factory to Receive New Life as Affordable Homes in Upstate NY
stories.excerpt: Developers have begun work on a new 80-unit affordable housing property on the site of a former factory in the Adirondack village of Tupper Lake, NY. The $46 million project will transform the long-vacant Oval Wood Dish Factory into modern apartments and more than 25,000 feet of commercial space, with residences affordable to households earning up to 90% of the Area Median Income. Housing Visions, Lahinch Group and Braxton Capital are developing the project, which will be all-electric, utilizing cold-climate heat pump technology for heating and cooling as well as a whole-building ventilation system. The Oval Wood Dish Factory development forms part of Governor Hochul’s $25 billion Housing Plan, which aims to create or preserve 100,000 affordable homes in New York over a five-year period. Oval Wood Dish Factory enjoys a mix of public and private financing, including Federal and State Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC) from New York State Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) that are expected to generate more than $17 million in equity. “Under Governor Hochul’s leadership, New York State is making the targeted investments needed to tackle our regional housing shortages head-on,” said Empire State Development President, CEO, & Commissioner Hope Knight in a statement. “The start of construction on the Oval Wood Dish development marks a transformative moment for Tupper Lake and the entire North Country.” The post Former Factory to Receive New Life as Affordable Homes in Upstate NY appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 80-unit affordable project, Tupper Lake NY, $46M funded by LIHTC equity ($17M+)
Part of NY State $25B Housing Plan targeting 100K affordable homes in 5 years
All-electric cold-climate heat pump design; mixed public/private financing structure
stories.summary: Housing Visions, Lahinch Group, and Braxton Capital are converting the Oval Wood Dish Factory in Tupper Lake, NY into an 80-unit affordable community with 25,000 sq ft of commercial space targeting households at 90% AMI. The $46M project leverages Low-Income Housing Tax Credits generating $17M+ in equity and is part of Governor Hochul's broader $25B affordable housing initiative. The all-electric development uses cold-climate heat pump technology and represents an adaptive reuse of a long-vacant industrial site.
stories.impact: This signals strong state-level capital commitment to affordable housing in upstate NY markets where demand outpaces supply. The availability of LIHTC equity and mixed financing structures lowers cost of capital for developers, making previously uneconomical projects feasible. However, this capital is constrained to affordable/workforce segments; market-rate development in smaller metros like Tupper Lake remains challenging, limiting total pipeline growth and suggesting selective market focus by institutional developers.

stories.title: Colliers Completes Sale of Healthcare Center in Twin Cities Metro
stories.excerpt: Colliers completed the sale of Eagan Medical Center, an outpatient facility located at 1185 Town Centre Drive in Eagan, Minnesota. The sale was led by the Colliers team of Tom O’Brien, Louis Suarez, Jordan Selbiger and Misty Bowe, who represented the seller, Tareen Development Partners (TDP), a Twin Cities-based real estate development firm focused on multifamily, mixed-use and community-driven projects across the Midwest. “TDP’s acquisition of the property in December 2024 marked the beginning of a value-add initiative,” said O’Brien. “By rebranding the former Town Centre Plaza as Eagan Medical Center, completing targeted improvements and driving leasing activity, TDP created a specialty healthcare destination that attracted strong investor interest.” The 43,419-square-foot medical office property is anchored by MNGI Digestive Health, Minnesota Urology and Tareen Dermatology, along with a complementary mix of specialty healthcare providers. Conveniently located near Interstates 35E and 494, the facility offers ample surface and underground parking. The post Colliers Completes Sale of Healthcare Center in Twin Cities Metro appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Tareen Development Partners (TDP) sold Eagan Medical Center, Twin Cities, specialty healthcare anchored
Value-add medical office conversion created 'specialty healthcare destination' for rapid exit
TDP remains active multifamily/mixed-use developer across Midwest with portfolio approach
stories.summary: Tareen Development Partners (TDP), a Twin Cities-based multifamily and mixed-use developer, acquired and repositioned the former Town Centre Plaza as Eagan Medical Center (43,419 sq ft) and sold it at profit. The property is anchored by MNGI Digestive Health, Minnesota Urology, and Tareen Dermatology with complementary specialty healthcare tenants and benefits from proximity to I-35E and I-494. Colliers brokered the sale, which demonstrated TDP's value-add execution and investor appetite for healthcare real estate.
stories.impact: This is a non-core transaction for a multifamily-focused developer—TDP's medical office flip demonstrates opportunistic capital allocation but signals no direct multifamily supply, demand, or cost implications for the Twin Cities metro. The exit velocity and buyer appetite for specialty healthcare indicate strong capital competition outside residential, which may reduce multifamily investor pool depth in the Twin Cities.

stories.title: Essex Realty Group Brokers Sale of 12-Unit MF in Tinley Park
stories.excerpt: Essex Realty Group completed the sale of 17114 71st Avenue, a 12-unit multifamily property in Tinley Park, Illinois, for $1.51 million.The property consists of ten two-bedroom, one-bathroom units and two one-bedroom, one-bathroom units. Two units have been fully renovated, while the remaining ten are in standard condition. The property had been owned by the same seller since 2001 and was acquired by an out-of-state investor with a growing portfolio in the Chicago area. With in-place rents substantially below market, the new owner plans to renovate the remaining units and push rents toward market levels.“This transaction highlights the strong investor appetite we’re seeing for value-add multifamily assets in Chicago’s suburban markets,” said Jimmy Donahue, Director at Essex Realty Group. “With rents well below market, this property gave the buyer a clear roadmap to drive returns, and we were glad to help facilitate a smooth transaction for both parties.” Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. bullets: 12-unit property, Tinley Park IL, sold for $1.51M by 23-year incumbent owner
Rents substantially below market; new out-of-state owner plans unit renovation & rent push
2 of 12 units already renovated; remaining 10 in standard condition
stories.summary: Essex Realty Group brokered the sale of a 12-unit multifamily property at 17114 71st Avenue in Tinley Park, Illinois for $1.51M. The property comprised ten 2-bed/1-bath and two 1-bed/1-bath units with only two fully renovated; the remainder in standard condition. The property had been owned by the same entity since 2001 and was acquired by an out-of-state investor planning value-add renovation and rent growth to market.
stories.impact: This signals market-rate rental opportunity in Tinley Park (southwest Chicago suburbs) where below-market in-place rents create arbitrage for value-add investors. The out-of-state buyer's interest and renovation plan indicate growing investor confidence in Chicago suburban multifamily, particularly in underserved small portfolios. However, the modest deal size ($1.51M, 12 units) reflects fragmented ownership and suggests limited institutional development appetite for suburban infill; consolidation and new supply remain constrained in this submarket.

stories.title: Ridge Capital Offloads Two Ukiah Apartment Complexes
stories.excerpt: Ridge Capital sold a two-apartment Northern California portfolio for $23.5 million. No buyer was disclosed. The apartment portfolio includes Sierra Sunset Village, a 68-unit development at 531 Capps Land and the Alderwood Apartments, a 53-unit venture at 1450 S. State Street in Ukiah. Sierra Sunset Village features mostly two-bedroom apartments with open floor plans, stainless steel appliances, hardwood-style flooring and central air conditioning. Community amenities include a pool, fitness center and an outdoor picnic area. Alderwood Apartments offers a mix of two- and three-bedroom floor plans onsite amenities that include a pool, covered garage parking and outdoor grilling areas. Zach LeBeouf and Anthony Pappageorge of Northmarq’s Walnut Creek, Calif., Investment Sales team represented the seller in the deal. The post Ridge Capital Offloads Two Ukiah Apartment Complexes appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Ridge Capital sold 121-unit Ukiah CA portfolio (Sierra Sunset 68-unit, Alderwood 53-unit) for $23.5M
Buyer undisclosed; properties feature standard amenities (pools, fitness, parking) and mixed unit mix
Northmarq brokered sale; transaction reflects Northern California secondary market liquidity
stories.summary: Ridge Capital sold a two-property apartment portfolio in Ukiah, California for $23.5M comprising Sierra Sunset Village (68 units, mostly 2-bed) and Alderwood Apartments (53 units, 2- and 3-bed mix). Both properties feature standard community amenities including pools, fitness centers, and covered parking. Northmarq's Walnut Creek office brokered the transaction; the buyer was not disclosed.
stories.impact: This signals liquidity and capital activity in Northern California secondary markets (Ukiah is rural inland), but lacks sufficient detail on market conditions, exit multiples, or buyer type to assess broader demand/supply dynamics. The sale itself suggests existing stabilized supply is trading, not new demand drivers or pipeline changes for the market. Without rent, occupancy, or buyer strategy data, the transaction's second-order effect is unclear.

stories.title: Advanced Materials Firm Nearly Doubles MA Footprint
stories.excerpt: CPS Technologies Corp., a NASDAQ-listed advanced materials company based in Massachusetts, is moving its headquarters and nearly doubling its footprint in the process. The company has signed an 80,000-square-foot lease for its new home in Attleboro, MA, less than 10 minutes from its current facility in Norton. CPS will move its operations including its corporate offices, manufacturing operations, and product development activities to the new address at 523 Pleasant St. The additional space will allow for increased production capacity and faster commercialization of new product lines, enabling CPS to tap increasing demand from industries such as defense, energy infrastructure, and artificial intelligence. Located near Providence, RI, the facility also provides room for future expansion. Colliers represented CPS in the lease, and Dacon Corporation is overseeing architectural and engineering design at the new facility. Image courtesy of Colliers. The post Advanced Materials Firm Nearly Doubles MA Footprint appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CPS Technologies Corp. leased 80K SF in Attleboro MA, nearly doubling footprint from Norton
Expansion driven by defense, energy infrastructure, AI demand; room for future growth
Colliers represented; Dacon handling design; facility near Providence RI enables future expansion
stories.summary: NASDAQ-listed CPS Technologies Corp., an advanced materials manufacturer based in Massachusetts, signed an 80,000-square-foot lease at 523 Pleasant Street in Attleboro, MA (less than 10 minutes from its current Norton facility). The expansion consolidates corporate offices, manufacturing, and product development and is driven by rising demand from defense, energy infrastructure, and AI sectors. The location near Providence, RI provides room for future expansion.
stories.impact: This is a corporate headquarters and manufacturing expansion in the Boston/Providence corridor, signaling strong employment growth in advanced materials/defense/AI sectors. In-migration of skilled workers and increased payroll for CPS and supply-chain vendors will strengthen rental demand in Attleboro and nearby Providence/Boston suburbs over the next 12–24 months. Multifamily developers should monitor Attleboro/North Attleboro submarkets for workforce housing demand; the AM-I-driven expansion cycle favors Class B/C apartments near manufacturing hubs within 20 miles of Boston.

stories.title: Tax-Exempt Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities Are Having a Moment
stories.excerpt: As the need for affordable housing in the U.S. grows, the tax-exempt commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) market is emerging as a potential financing tool to deliver more homes. New federal rules and greater attention from ratings agencies and top-tier banks are helping the growth of the burgeoning structure. Tax-exempt affordable housing securitizations have taken flight of late after years of largely flying under the radar, according to Ryan Paszczykowski, head of structured investing at Systima Capital Management. Tax-exempt CMBS deals occurred on an occasional basis back in the 2000s, but the structure began to develop consistently in the late 2010s when Citigroup and Freddie Mac rolled out programs offering credit risk transfer securities backed by tax-exempt loans issued by state or local housing agencies. The tax-exempt structures of these deals offer lower costs of capital than standard taxable CMBS or traditional affordable housing loans backed by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac. Freddie Mac then launched a multifamily loan program in 2017 securitized by tax-exempt loans tied to properties receiving new-issue 4 percent Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTCs) and expanded its outreach of the offering in late 2024 through a new registration system. Now, the product is starting to take hold as a securitized offering in the municipal debt space at a time when there is increased support nationally to find financial solutions for America’s housing challenges. The deals have become more attractive to investors in a higher interest rate climate since the value of tax-exempt debt stays higher as rates remain elevated while also serving as an attractive option for high-yield investors who are drawn to collateral protections like the federally backed LIHTCs. A recent deal that Systima itself was involved in underscores the increased demand. bullets: Tax-exempt CMBS emerging as financing tool for affordable multifamily; consistent growth since late 2010s
Freddie Mac 2017 multifamily program ties tax-exempt loans to new-issue 4% LIHTC properties
Structures offer lower cost of capital than taxable CMBS or traditional Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac loans
stories.summary: Tax-exempt commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) are emerging as a financing tool for affordable housing development following new federal rules and increased attention from ratings agencies and top-tier banks. The structure grew consistently in the late 2010s after Citigroup and Freddie Mac rolled out credit risk transfer programs backed by state/local housing agency loans. Freddie Mac launched a dedicated multifamily securitization program in 2017 for properties receiving 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, offering lower capital costs than taxable alternatives.
stories.impact: Tax-exempt CMBS reduces the cost of capital for affordable multifamily development, expanding the addressable market for LIHTC projects that were previously constrained by financing costs. This lowers hurdle rates and increases feasibility for new construction and adaptive reuse of affordable units in secondary/tertiary markets. Multifamily developers should monitor Freddie Mac's tax-exempt program expansion and state housing agency partnership opportunities to lock in lower rates; this is a structural tailwind for affordable product and may reduce competitive pressure on market-rate development in strong-demand metros as capital redirects to LIHTC-eligible deals.

stories.title: Dermatology Chain LaserAway Adds 15th NYC Location on the Upper East Side
stories.excerpt: Skin care, hair removal and body wellness services provider LaserAway is getting ready to open its 15th New York City location on Manhattan’s Upper East Side, Commercial Observer has learned. LaserAway signed a 10-year lease for 1,800 square feet on the ground floor of a mixed-use property at 242 East 86th Street, according to a source close to the deal. Asking rent was $165 per square foot. The Yorkville property is owned by the LLC 244 East 86th Street, which is linked to Shore Assets, according to property records. Michael Miller from The Shopping Center Group represented LaserAway in this deal, while Darrell Rubens and Richard Gelber from Newmark represented the landlord. Rubens and Gelber declined to comment, while Miller did not immediately respond to a request for comment. LaserAway offers clients several services including laser hair removal, Botox injections, cool sculpting, facials, tattoo removal and micro-needling. The company already has an East Side location at 1430 Second Avenue, according to its website. LaserAway’s other New York City locations include 118 Court Street in Brooklyn Heights, 35 East 19th Street in the Flatiron District, and 36-07 30th Avenue in Astoria, Queens. Other outposts are in Morningside Heights, the Meatpacking District, Tribeca and near Lincoln Center. Located on East 86th Street between Second and Third avenues, 242 East 86th Street is a 55,158-square-foot, mid-rise mixed-use property. The building was constructed in 1920 and renovated in 2003, according to Loopnet.com. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: LaserAway opened 15th NYC location, Upper East Side, 1,800 SF ground floor, $165/SF asking rent
10-year lease at 242 East 86th Street; Yorkville market shows service/retail demand density
LaserAway expanding rapidly; already operates second East Side location at 1430 Second Avenue
stories.summary: Skin care and wellness services provider LaserAway signed a 10-year lease for 1,800 square feet on the ground floor of 242 East 86th Street on Manhattan's Upper East Side. The asking rent was $165 per square foot. This is LaserAway's 15th NYC location and second on the Upper East Side (a second location operates at 1430 Second Avenue), reflecting the company's rapid expansion and market confidence in the Yorkville neighborhood.
stories.impact: LaserAway's rapid retail expansion in high-rent Manhattan submarkets (15 locations citywide, multiple Upper East Side outposts) signals strong consumer services demand and lease-signing velocity in premium retail corridors. This indicates stable or growing foot traffic and spending power in Manhattan neighborhoods, a secondary-order signal of strong residential demand and population retention in these areas. However, this is primarily a retail/ground-floor signal, not a multifamily supply or demand driver; it does not directly affect apartment development feasibility or pipeline in NYC.

stories.title: Nuveen Green Capital Closes $173M C-PACE Loan on Miami-Area Condos Project
stories.excerpt: The continued strength of Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) debt as a construction financing tool has made a big splash in South Florida. Miami developer Shoma Group has landed a $172.5 million C-PACE loan from Nuveen Green Capital to develop its Shoma Bay mixed-use condominium waterfront project in North Bay Village, Fla., Commercial Observer can first report. This transaction provides further evidence of the power of C-PACE to provide accretive financing for large-scale assets such as Shoma Bay,” Ryan Doyle, senior director of originations, at Nuveen Green Capital, said in a statement. “The project is particularly impactful, as Nuveen Green Capital served as the sole capital provider for this development, which ranks among the five largest C-PACE-financed projects in the state of Florida.” Doyle originated the loan with a Nuveen Green Capital team that also featured Christopher Lawton, head of originations, along with Brendan Moore, director, and Tyler Amano, associate director. One source familiar with the transaction said it’s notable because there’s no other debt provider in the capital stack — just the C-PACE loan, condo sales deposits and equity. Located at 1850 John F. Kennedy Causeway 10 miles northeast of Downtown Miami, the 24-story Shoma Bay development will comprise 333 condo units and retail space anchored by a 36,000-square-foot Publix supermarket. Community amenities will include a rooftop pool deck, a wellness spa, a two-story fitness center, a padel court and coworking spaces. Newmark negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Anthony Orso, Clifford Welden, Daniel Matz and Henry Stimler. “Shoma Bay is an exceptional project that reflects the continued evolution of North Bay Village into one of South Florida’s most dynamic waterfront communities,” Orso said in a statement. Shoma Group did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nuveen Green Capital closed $172.5M C-PACE loan for Shoma Bay mixed-use condo project, North Bay Village FL
Sole capital provider; ranks among 5 largest C-PACE deals in Florida; construction financing model
C-PACE emerges as primary construction debt tool for large South Florida residential/mixed-use projects
stories.summary: Nuveen Green Capital closed a $172.5M C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy) loan with Shoma Group for the Shoma Bay mixed-use waterfront condominium project in North Bay Village, Florida. Nuveen served as sole capital provider, making this one of the five largest C-PACE-financed projects in Florida. The transaction demonstrates C-PACE's power as a primary construction financing mechanism for large-scale residential mixed-use assets in South Florida.
stories.impact: C-PACE is filling a construction financing gap in South Florida, enabling mega-scale residential/mixed-use development that traditional construction lenders or agency financing may not fully underwrite. This expands the feasible pipeline for large-format developments and lowers cost of capital relative to taxable construction debt. Multifamily developers in South Florida should incorporate C-PACE structuring into underwriting for new construction with green/efficiency components; the availability of large, sole-capital providers like Nuveen lowers deal risk and accelerates feasibility for projects in Miami, Broward, and Palm Beach counties. This is a structural tailwind for South Florida residential pipeline.

stories.title: Related Ross Buys Land for Major Mixed-Use Dev in Florida
stories.excerpt: Billionaire Stephen Ross has closed on a land acquisition to build a major, open-air mixed-use development in Wellington, a village in Palm Beach County, Fla., renowned for its equestrian scene. Related Ross, the developer’s namesake firm, paid $28.3 million for a 32-acre site at 10400 Stribling Way, just east of State Road 7, property records show. The planned development, called Village Landing, is set to include a 180-room hotel and over 300,000 square feet of retail, office and restaurant space, all connected by six plazas. “Our goal is to create a village center that complements what is already special about Wellington while adding the everyday amenities, restaurants, experiences and connections that are designed to serve the western communities of Palm Beach County,” Kevin Ryan, executive vice president of Related Ross, said in a statement. Starwood Property Trust supplied a $29.1 million loan. Construction is expected to commence in the fall. The western portion of the site, spanning about 44 acres, will be turned into a private grade school, operated by ElevateED. The land sale is expected to close in October, per a representative for Related Ross. The combined 71-acre parcel is part of the Acme Improvement District, which was controlled by the Village of Wellington. In 1953, the Florida Legislature created the special district to manage water drainage and infrastructure development. Village Landing marks Related Ross’ first ground-up development outside of West Palm Beach since launching in 2024 and becoming the city’s biggest office owner. Ross’s goal is to turn West Palm Beach into a leading business hub and attract high-profile tech and finance companies. The West Palm Beach-based firm is building two more office buildings after securing a $772 million construction loan package last year. Two luxury condo developments are under construction. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Related Ross acquired 32-acre land parcel, Wellington FL (Palm Beach County), $28.3M for Village Landing
Mixed-use development: 180-room hotel, 300K+ SF retail/office/restaurant, 6 plazas; fall construction start
Starwood Property Trust provided $29.1M loan; site has expansion capacity east of SR-7
stories.summary: Related Ross closed a $28.3M land acquisition for 32 acres at 10400 Stribling Way in Wellington, Florida (Palm Beach County) to develop Village Landing, a major open-air mixed-use project. The planned development includes a 180-room hotel and over 300,000 square feet of retail, office, and restaurant space connected by six plazas, with construction expected to commence in fall. Starwood Property Trust provided a $29.1M construction loan; the site has room for future expansion.
stories.impact: Related's $28.3M land acquisition and immediate construction financing in Wellington (western Palm Beach County, equestrian-focused affluent community) signals strong developer confidence in western Palm Beach County's growth trajectory and experiential retail/hospitality demand. This is primarily mixed-use retail/hotel, not multifamily, but it indicates capital flow and infrastructure investment in a secondary Palm Beach County submarket. This could signal indirect multifamily opportunity—residential demand typically follows mixed-use/retail anchors in affluent suburban markets. Developers should monitor Wellington/western Palm Beach County for residential land parcels and Class A multifamily development opportunities as Village Landing construction advances and retail/hospitality anchors mature.

stories.title: Investor General Atlantic to Anchor Related’s 625 Madison Avenue in 150K-SF Deal
stories.excerpt: Related Companies just nabbed an anchor tenant for its under-construction office tower at 625 Madison Avenue in Manhattan’s Plaza District, the developer announced Tuesday. General Atlantic, a global investment firm, has inked a long-term lease to occupy more than 150,000 square feet across five floors at the planned 53-story office tower, which is slated to open in 2029. The firm will use the space for its more than 330 New York-based employees, who represent about one-third of the company’s global workforce. “General Atlantic has always taken a long-term view, and our new headquarters is an investment in the firm’s future,” Bill Ford, chairman and CEO of General Atlantic, said in a statement. “It will be a place that brings our people and global community together, strengthens the connections that are central to who we are, and gives us room to grow for many decades to come.” The exact length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for Class A office space in the Plaza District was $97.23 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to Colliers data. Related did not disclose the names of the brokers who worked on this deal. “When we began designing 625 Madison, General Atlantic was exactly the kind of prestigious and ambitious firm we had in mind as an anchor tenant because of the value they place on investment and operational excellence, collaboration and long-term relationships,” Jeff Blau, CEO of Related, said in a statement. “This will be a building of industry leaders, and we are thrilled to have General Atlantic on board and look forward to delivering an exceptional new headquarters for their team.” In tandem with General Atlantic’s lease, private equity firm Veritas Capital has also seemed to secure new office space at 625 Madison Avenue. bullets: General Atlantic leased 150K+ SF across 5 floors at Related's 625 Madison Avenue, opening 2029
Anchor tenant represents 330+ NYC employees (~1/3 of firm's global workforce); 53-story office tower
Long-term lease; Plaza District average Class A asking rent $97.23/SF; no rent/length terms disclosed
stories.summary: Related Companies announced that global investment firm General Atlantic has signed a long-term lease to occupy more than 150,000 square feet across five floors at the company's under-construction 53-story office tower at 625 Madison Avenue in Manhattan's Plaza District. The space will house General Atlantic's 330+ New York-based employees (approximately one-third of the firm's global workforce). The tower is slated to open in 2029; exact lease length and rental rate were not disclosed.
stories.impact: General Atlantic's 150K+ SF office anchor at 625 Madison Avenue signals strong institutional investor commitment to Manhattan office post-COVID and confidence in Plaza District (Midtown East) recovery. However, this is a back-office/corporate HQ lease, not a direct multifamily demand driver. The broader implication: if Plaza District office recovers and attracts major relocations, workforce in-migration could support residential demand in Upper East Side and Midtown East apartment markets in 2027–2030. Multifamily developers should monitor office anchor activity in Manhattan CBD submarkets as a leading indicator of residential demand inflection; Plaza District office recovery would justify new luxury/Class A multifamily supply in adjacent residential neighborhoods.
